subject: castle-walls-v2
label: Castle curtain wall, towers and gate — flat elevation at 1:1, sized against the cliff
notes: THIS FIXES A BLOCKING DEFECT. The shipped kit contains TWO INCOMPATIBLE PROJECTIONS: towers, corners and the gate arch are drawn flat (0px lean), while castle-wall-straight-front (-96px lean over 115 rows), castle-wall-straight-side (-75px) and castle-wall-connector-tower (-42px) are drawn as ~40-degree diagonals. Proof: scripts/sprite-lab/review/castle-kit/wall-projection-defect.png

ROOT CAUSE, per environment-art-director 2026-08-06: the diagonal pieces came from /create-tiles-pro with tile_feature 'building', which produces a RAKING WALL-STRIP projection. That is incompatible with /create-image-pixen view:'side' elevation renders. Mixing two endpoints inside one structural family is what caused the defect. COMMIT TO ONE ENDPOINT PER FAMILY — this config is entirely /create-image-pixen, the same route that produced the cliff bands.

SCALE IS DERIVED, NOT GUESSED. Hero 100px on 32px ground tiles. Cliff face 256px (2.56x hero) — Raheem sized that himself in the editor. Wall is 288px so it is 32px TALLER than the cliff it stands on and shares a datum with the 288px cliff stair. Tower is 384px — 96px / 33% above the wall, because a castle whose towers match its walls has no silhouette. The old kit had walls at 0.93-1.15x hero and towers at 1.29-1.39x: shorter than the staircase, which is why the castle never read as a castle.

WALL MUST NOT MERGE WITH THE CLIFF. A 288px wall directly above a 256px cliff is 544px of continuous stone. Three separations, all stated positively in the prompts rather than as negations: (1) VALUE — the cliff darkens toward its base; the wall is flat-lit with no gradient. (2) HUE — cliff is warm grey-and-honey sandstone with moss; wall is cool quarried blue-grey with mortar joints and explicitly no moss and no honey tone. (3) SILHOUETTE — cliff has an irregular organic top lip; the wall has a dead-straight coursed top with crenellations. The silhouette break at the join is what actually sells 'built structure on natural rock'.

DO NOT RUN ramp_transfer.py ON THESE. Logged error, 2026-08-06: a carved stone pillar was palette-matched onto the natural cliff ramp and vanished into it. Raheem: 'How would the pillar stand out from the cliff face? That makes absolutely no art directive.' Carved-versus-natural IS the visual argument for why a castle sits on a cliff instead of merging with it. ramp_transfer is reserved for DRESSING ONLY — moss at a wall base, ivy, grass on crenellations — region-constrained. Never the base stone.

TILING IS SEAM-AUTHORED, NOT MIRRORED. Mirroring is right for organic cliff faces and symmetric endcaps. It is wrong for a coursed wall: mirroring a directional piece is what turned the stair into a symmetric arch. So the straight wall is authored with an EVEN, DIRECTION-AGNOSTIC block pattern and no off-centre features, and any asymmetric detail (buttress, banner bracket) is a DISCRETE MODULE dropped into the repeat — the same logic that made the stair pillar solve the stair/cliff butt-join.

CORNERS ARE THE ONE EXCEPTION TO PURE ELEVATION. A corner must show two faces, so it gets a shallow oblique — pinned at ~18 degrees, not the ~40 that caused the defect. Raheem approved the shallow angle as a default.
GATE ARCH IS NOT REGENERATED. castle-gate-arch-open-healthy already follows the correct flat elevation convention. Per the director, reuse it rather than re-buying it.
